correctness.rationale: Deterministic WEFX is equivalent to the pairwise weighted count inequalities; sparse counts form a uniform hypersimplex; nonempty counts are selected Adams divisor-score prefixes. Exact tie-hypersimplex convexity gives the iff ex-ante test. Positive normalized weights plus tied integer multiples force rationality; repeated rational score bands prove period b. A two-agent length-one interval gives exactly the residue classes. The packaged independent exact-rational checker reproduced raw feasible outcomes and independently solved finite lottery feasibility. Infinite statements rest on the displayed proof, not the finite checks.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating full text provides a two-agent counterexample but no complete compatibility criterion. Classical Adams ranking is explicitly credited. Examined random-apportionment and dividend methods do not state or directly imply convex-hull membership of a fixed Adams support with its arithmetic consequences. Genuine remaining risk: an unindexed or implicit apportionment theorem may already cover some or all of the statement.
residual_risks: The full Chakraborty et al. (2019) original was not inspected; a hidden fixed-Adams convex hull implication cannot be ruled out.
An equivalent exact Adams-support unbiased lottery theorem may appear in inaccessible or unindexed apportionment literature.
Comparison of statements from accessible primary full text, not uniqueness of all literature, underlies this provisional originality assessment.

value.rationale: A recent weighted-chores best-of-both-worlds obstruction motivates a complete criterion rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The priority tie polytope distinguishes feasible lotteries; rationality and periodicity reveal an arithmetic phenomenon even under homogeneous costs; the sharp two-agent congruence makes infinitely many instances decidable by a single residue check. The domain and limitations are explicit and the results do not merely restate the Adams algorithm.
